Five Compounding Failure Modes

1. Benchmark Prompt Mismatch (The Silent Turo Assumption) Specification Gap
The benchmark evaluation interceptor was registered to listen strictly on turo.com/.*/search. However, the user prompt provided to the agent merely said: "Book a car rental on June 20 from Toronto to Niagara Falls, pick up at 9am and return the car by 6pm, compact car". Since the prompt did not prescribe Turo, Claude Opus autonomously reasoned: "Let me go to a popular car rental comparison site or a specific rental company. I'll try kayak.com or similar." This doomed the trajectory from Turn 10 with a 0% chance of intercepting.
2. Regional Route Friction: Zero One-Way Rental Availability Domain Reality
Toronto to Niagara Falls is an inter-city regional route (~130 km). In traditional car rental fleets, one-way drop-offs between municipal branches either carry hefty drop fees or are outright unavailable for single-day rentals. When Kayak returned "No matching results were found", Claude Opus became trapped in a reasoning loop over whether "Toronto to Niagara Falls" implied a one-way trip or a round-trip excursion.
3. Cloud Runner Geolocation Poisoning Environment Bias
The CDP browser instance ran in an AWS datacenter. Kayak's IP-geolocation engine repeatedly resolved the runner's location to "Hoffman, Illinois, United States". Each time Claude attempted to construct direct query URLs or reset the form, Kayak's client-side state clobbered Toronto with Hoffman, IL.
4. Anti-Bot Defense Interference (AWS WAF Bot Control) Security Wall
Pivoting to rentalcars.com at Turn 100 hit an active AWS WAF deployment (edge.sdk.awswaf.com). The WAF client telemetry analyzed mouse/keystroke cadence. Synthetic CDP type and keydown events were suppressed or flagged, causing the pickup location autocomplete dropdown to continually display "No Results Found" for "Toronto".
5. Cascading Tool Timeouts & Benchmark Hard Expiry Infrastructure
At Turn 87, OpenClaw's CDP gateway timed out with an internal message: "timed out. Restart the OpenClaw gateway... Do NOT retry the browser tool". Claude successfully recovered by switching to screenshot actions. However, at Turn 120, an Anthropic internal server 500 error struck. While retried, the benchmark's 30-minute hard ceiling was reached at 1,828 seconds, terminating the session.

AWS WAF Bot Control Forensics

During Phase 4, the agent navigated to https://www.rentalcars.com/ to bypass Kayak's zero-inventory deadlock. Immediately upon page load, Rentalcars initiated a handshake with AWS WAF's edge SDK at d8c14d4960ca.edge.sdk.awswaf.com:

  • /telemetry (11 POSTs): Transmitted browser canvas fingerprints, navigator plugins, and CDP automation markers.
  • /inputs?client=browser (1 GET): Active monitoring script attached to DOM input event listeners.
  • /mp_verify (1 POST): Cryptographic validation of user human interaction cadence.

Because OpenClaw was typing via synthetic CDP keyboard dispatches (without organic mouse wander or human interval variance), the WAF suppressed the location autocomplete endpoint. Claude's keystrokes for Toronto yielded "No Results Found", trapping the agent in an input-clearing retry loop until the 30-minute benchmark ceiling terminated the session.

Benchmark Design Takeaways
1. Domain declaration: If a test case requires a specific service (e.g. Turo), that name must be in the prompt.
2. WAF isolation: Live web tasks should use controlled mock sandbox proxies to avoid headless agent blocking.
3. Timeout recovery: When agents hit repeated DOM input failures, they should trigger alternative provider triage.
